I am old now, 83 years, and my strength is not what it was. This rice plot I have worked for many years, and I do as my family has always done — we plant the rice seeds we saved from last harvest, and we use the cow manure we have at home because chemical fertilizer costs too much money for a widow like me. My grandchildren and children help me in the field since I cannot bend long in the mud, and when the transplanting and harvest time comes, we call some neighbors and pay them a little. The rains here in Ruvuma are usually enough for the rice, so I do not have any irrigation — I depend on God and the sky.
